ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of a linear function intersects the x-axis at point A and the y-axis at point B. What is the length of $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $A(-6, 0)$ and $B(0, 2)$, \\
$\therefore OA=6$ and $OB=2$, \\
In the right-angled triangle $AOB$, $AB=\sqrt{OA^{2}+OB^{2}}=\sqrt{6^{2}+2^{2}}=\boxed{2\sqrt{10}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Given $A(-6, 0)$ and $B(0, 2)$, $\therefore OA=6$ and $OB=2$. In the right-angled triangle $AOB$, $AB=\sqrt{OA^{2}+OB^{2}}=\sqrt{6^{2}+2^{2}}=\boxed{2\sqrt{10}}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a rectangular coordinate system; an oblique straight line intersects the x-axis at point A, A is to the left of the origin O, and the abscissa is labeled as -6; the straight line intersects the y-axis at point B, B is above the origin O, and the ordinate is labeled as 2. Therefore A=(-6,0), B=(0,2). Reasoning: OA is the horizontal distance from 0 to -6, so OA=6; OB is the vertical distance from 0 to 2, so OB=2. Because the x-axis and the y-axis are perpendicular, triangle AOB is a right triangle, and AB is the hypotenuse. By the Pythagorean theorem, AB=sqrt(6^2+2^2)=sqrt(36+4)=sqrt(40)=2sqrt(10).
